quotes.text: ClinEnv is built from MIMIC-IV v3.1 ( Johnson et al., 2023a ) and MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2 ( Johnson et al., 2023b ).
Because every stage is built deterministically from logged events, the ground truth can always be traced back to the originating row.

rationale: Dataset names and versions (MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2) are given, the platform is PhysioNet, and events are keyed by subject_id and hadm_id. Appendix D states ground truth traces to the originating row, which is the task-to-source route.

quotes.text: ClinEnv is derived from MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Note, which are de-identified and distributed through PhysioNet under a credentialed data use agreement

rationale: Origin (MIMIC-IV, one US academic medical center) and terms (credentialed DUA) are stated. Consent or IRB status, or an explicit 'not required', is not stated, and no collection method is described beyond the source EHR, so the score is 1. The sentence that the data come from clinical sources for research use adds nothing specific.

quotes.text: Decisions (total) | 26,043

rationale: Descriptive dataset statistics are given (stage and decision counts, type mix, distinct codes and drugs, stages per case). No comparison against a named target population is reported, and the limitations section concedes a single-center source.

searched: S1 (ethics, limitations, results, appendices), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4/S5 prompts and scorers. No dedicated unsafe-output test or bias test is reported. The Appendix Z sentence about subgroup reporting by sex and race is slice reporting (A10), not a dedicated bias test, and no results appear.

quotes.text: the test split is held out and distributed only through gated access
we measured verbatim overlap between the test tasks and a public web corpus, finding no exact matches

rationale: A developer-side control (held-out split with gated access; a canary string is also stated in Phase C) is paired with a measured verbatim-overlap check against a web corpus. This meets the two-part anchor.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search.
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces

rationale: The paper states the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time and names mechanisms (no web access, retrieval restricted to the task environment, labels not public). Appendix C.2 adds that coded outcomes and discharge summaries are not passively exposed.

quotes.text: The environment is frozen at release: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions
no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test

Maps drug names to ATC codes via the public RxNorm API (no key required),

rationale: Appendix Z reports a frozen, pinned environment with no external calls other than the model under test, which meets the top anchor as reported. Code shows live RxNorm API calls at scoring time and unpinned env_model names in config, so a contradiction flag is raised for verification.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.
All 120 reference implementations received correct grades.

rationale: A scripted reference solution is run through the grader and the result is reported. The count of 120 sits oddly beside 9,297 stages, which is noted, but the anchor is met as written.

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

contradiction_quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged
Per-type Hungarian algorithm assigns each GT item to at most one submission.

rationale: Appendix Z reports a grader that checks changed and unchanged state, so NA does not apply to the packet as written and the top anchor is met. The code scorer only matches submissions to ground-truth items and never inspects record state, so a contradiction flag is raised.

quotes.text: Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: An empirical random-agent rate (3.1%) is reported. The referenced appendix tables for per-metric baselines do not appear in the packet.

quotes.text: Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: A random-action agent's score is reported as covering all tasks ('across tasks'), which meets the anchor. A do-nothing agent is not separately reported.

quotes.text: validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3%

rationale: The benchmark validates its own evaluator on 200 physician-labelled outputs and reports agreement (94%) and error rates (FP 3%, FN 8%). This meets the top anchor.

quotes.text: Reliability measurement: each task executed eight times.

contradiction_quotes.text: Reliability measurement: each task executed eight times.
each task is run three times

rationale: S1 states a repeated-run policy (eight runs) but gives no seed or temperature on S1-S3. Temperature 0 appears only in code. Code comments disagree with S1 (three runs, and also five runs with temperature 0.7), so a contradiction flag is raised.

quotes.text: Statistical testing of the two top-performing models employed paired permutation testing with p = 0.02.
Model scores include 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

rationale: Bootstrap CIs are reported and a paired permutation test is applied to the headline comparison of the top two models. The vague claim of small variance across settings adds nothing.

quotes.text: each task executed eight times

contradiction_quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds

rationale: Run count per task (eight) is stated on S1. No seed or decoding controls and no independence statement appear on S1-S3; those are only in code comments, which conflict with S1 (three or five runs), hence the flag.

quotes.text: Model scores include 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

rationale: CIs are reported on model scores, and Figure 2 uses standard-error bands. The resampling unit (task, patient or run) is not named, and clustering of stages within admissions or patients is not addressed.

quotes.text: We report pass^8 (share of tasks solved in all 8 runs) and agreement rates of the final environment state across these eight runs.

contradiction_quotes.text: each task is run three times

rationale: An all-runs metric (pass^8) and final-state agreement across eight runs are stated, with the run count. Code comments give a different run count (three or five), so a contradiction flag is raised.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. S1 gives family-level names (GPT-5.4, Llama-3.1-70B, Claude-Sonnet-4.6 planner) without snapshot IDs, and S4 differs (planner.json uses gpt-5.4, runtime.json uses deepseek-chat), which counts as absent. No decoding parameters or harness commit are stated on S1-S3. The README dated default ID covers only one model.

quotes.text: ask_patient | Interactive | Query patient agent
Ask the patient a question about their symptoms, history, or concerns.
The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.

rationale: Every tool has a JSON schema in the agent-visible tool definitions, and Table 3 gives function and mode. Read versus write is distinguished on S1 and return semantics are partly documented (null lab response, duplicates ignored). The S5 descriptions do not state read/write effects or sandboxing explicitly, so S5 reach is false. The generic sentence that the agent can use tools adds nothing.

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses.
disclosed both in the paper and in the tool descriptions visible to the agent

The code shows no fixed-placeholder tools (agents are LLM-backed), and none of the S5 tool descriptions carries a stub disclosure, so S5 reach is recorded as false and a contradiction flag is raised.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.
The agent prompt states that writes are sandboxed.

contradiction_quotes.text: unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.

The scorer is a plain F1 with no write penalty, and the S5 prompts shown do not state sandboxing, so S5 reach is false and a contradiction flag is raised.

quotes.text: validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3%
a judge is given the complete readview

rationale: Grader inputs are named (structured submissions mapped to ICD/ATC, and an LLM judge over the dialogue trace for process metrics). The paper gives a rationale for the mapping and process design. Validation uses 200 human-labelled outputs with FP and FN rates, which meets (iii).

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: Leakage controls on web and retrieval access, a private held-out split with hidden labels, and a canary string on released tasks are all stated on S1.

quotes.text: Diagnosis-only stages score far above management stages.
per patient subgroup by sex and race, and each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: Results by decision type (Dx, Rx, Proc, Table 6) are reported. Appendix Z states that results are reported per patient subgroup by sex and race with the number of cases per slice. The subgroup tables themselves are not in the packet, so this rests on the stated sentence.

quotes.text: ClinEnv is derived from MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-Note, which are de-identified and distributed through PhysioNet under a credentialed data use agreement

rationale: Records are stated as real de-identified MIMIC-IV data with a credentialed DUA and a PhysioNet credential requirement. Data terms are stated as PhysioNet's, separate from any code licence. No synthetic origin is inferred.
